title: Automatic clients have only link-local addresses
scenario: A fresh LAN has one R1 router and several SLAAC-capable PCs. All physical links are up. R1 answers a manually configured PC at its global-form interface address. Automatic PCs receive no usable global prefix or default router. There is no other router and no DHCPv6 server. Excerpts are representative.

exhibits.title: Complete relevant R1 configuration
exhibits.text:
no ipv6 unicast-routing
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ipv6 address 2001:db8:acad:1::1/64
 ipv6 address fe80::1 link-local
 no shutdown
No RA-suppression configuration.

exhibits.title: PC observations
exhibits.text:
Manual PC 2001:db8:acad:1::10/64 can ping 2001:db8:acad:1::1.
Automatic PCs show only link-local addresses; no RA is observed.

question: Which correction addresses the shown missing prerequisite?
options: Enable ipv6 unicast-routing globally on R1.
Add ipv6 enable to the already IPv6-addressed interface.
Replace its manual global address with an EUI-64-derived address.
Set the RA managed flag without changing global forwarding.
explanation: The complete configuration lacks global IPv6 router operation. Interface addressing already enables local IPv6 processing; EUI-64 is an address-generation choice, and the managed flag describes DHCPv6 behavior. None supplies the missing forwarding/advertising prerequisite.
fix:
```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ipv6 unicast-routing
R1(config)# end
R1# show ipv6 interface gigabitethernet0/0
```
Confirm the /64 and RA settings. Allow clients to receive a new RA, or refresh Automatic mode if supported. Verify their actual prefix and learned gateway, then test numeric-address connectivity. A DHCPv6 address server is not required for this SLAAC exercise.

title: The documented gateway was never assigned
scenario: On an isolated LAN, PCs use 2001:db8:acad:2::1 as their manual gateway. The router interface is up and its current configuration uses EUI-64. A PC can ping the actual derived address but cannot resolve the documented ::1 address. No other device owns ::1.

exhibits.title: Complete Gi0/1 address settings
exhibits.text:
ipv6 address 2001:db8:acad:2::/64 eui-64
ipv6 address fe80::1 link-local

question: Which diagnosis matches the evidence?
options: EUI-64 also created ::1; refreshing the neighbor cache is the only required repair.
The PC prefix must be widened until it includes every router address.
The expected manual gateway is absent; the derived address has a different suffix.
The router link-local address must have the same suffix as its derived global address.
explanation: The complete address display contains the derived address but not ::1. A working ping to the actual address supports local connectivity. Cache refresh or a wider prefix cannot assign the missing address, and manually assigned link-local and derived global suffixes can differ.
fix:
Choose and document a consistent addressing plan. To retain the intended ::1 gateway in this isolated lab, add it explicitly:
```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/1
R1(config-if)# ipv6 address 2001:db8:acad:2::1/64
R1(config-if)# end
R1# show ipv6 interface gigabitethernet0/1
```
This adds the manual address alongside the existing derived address; it does not remove it. Verify no duplicate is reported and test the configured gateway. Alternatively, update the manual PC gateway to the correctly scoped fe80::1, then verify that chosen design before saving.
